key_results.text: Release v2 with streaks and smart reminders on both App Store and Google Play
Grow monthly active users from 4,000 to 7,000
Raise average store rating from 3.9 to 4.4
Conclude a two-variant pricing experiment with a written decision memo

input.context: Solo indie developer (Flutter + Firebase) running Habitly, a habit-tracking app with about 4,000 monthly active users and a freemium subscription. About 4 hours per workday on this OKR.

must_cover: Finalize v2 scope and specs for streaks and smart reminders
Beta test (TestFlight / internal track) and fix blocking bugs
Submit the release to both stores
Triage top crash clusters from crash reporting
Fix the top crashes and verify the crash-free rate in beta or production
Launch campaign for v2 (social posts, communities, press kit or store listing refresh)
Referral or re-engagement push for dormant users
In-app rating prompt shown at positive moments
Reply to negative reviews and address the top complaints
Improve the paywall or trial offer
Experiment design (hypothesis, variants, duration, success metric)
Run the experiment for a fixed period
Analyze results and write the decision memo

expected.grader_notes: The v2 launch campaign should depend on the store release; the pricing experiment should depend on conversion tracking. O3-KR1 and O3-KR2 share paywall variant work: building the variants twice counts as duplication. Store review waiting time is calendar time, not work hours, so it must not appear as a multi-hour task. Three objectives with strict priority means lower-priority growth and monetization tasks come after the v2 release chain.
